account-wide-agent-grant-01.graded_text: The design gives the agent connection a scope covering every workspace the person belongs to now or later plus documents shared with them individually, says the consent screen states that scope, and does not make the person pick one organization per connection.

votes.e: The scope itself is right. docs/workspace-access.md:73 "one OAuth connection covers every workspace the person belongs to". :63 "*all my workspaces*, which is derived live from membership, so joining a new client workspace needs no reconnect". Shared documents are included through :103 "across all your workspaces and documents shared with you" and Assumption 5 (:193). Nothing asks the person to pick an org per connection (:79 "No per-workspace resources or paths"). But the design never says the consent screen states this scope. The only mention of consent is :75 "the usual pattern of an organization-scoped grant, where consent selects one workspace", which describes the rejected pattern. The consent text for the chosen grant is never specified, so this required part is missing.

account-wide-agent-grant-02.graded_text: Every tool call resolves the target workspace or document and checks live membership, role, and individual share on the server at call time. A single organization claim in a token is not treated as proof of access to any other workspace.

votes.e: docs/workspace-access.md:73 "Each tool call names the workspace or document it acts on, and the gate checks membership for that specific target on that call". :17 "Roles, membership, and agent reach are read live at each call". :65 "allowed = (role grants it OR share grants it) AND ...". :81 "If the token carries an organization claim, it is **ignored for authorization**. It never selects or limits a workspace."

account-wide-agent-grant-03.graded_text: The create tool takes an explicit destination workspace ID, and the server verifies the caller may create in that workspace before creating. The design does not say a client-supplied workspace ID must never be used.

votes.e: docs/workspace-access.md:115 "`workspace` is **required** and takes a workspace ID ... an omitted workspace is a validation error". The server checks it: :14 "Selecting never grants. A workspace you are not a member of is refused even if you name it", the role table at :51-55 grants create only to Owner and Editor, and :128 refuses Viewers. Nothing forbids client-supplied IDs: :14 lists "a tool argument" as a valid way to select the target.

account-wide-agent-grant-04.graded_text: Removing a membership or an individual share takes effect for an already connected agent without reconnecting.

votes.e: docs/workspace-access.md:83 "Removing someone from a workspace cuts their agent off from it on the very next call, because membership is read live." Shares are covered by :17 "Nothing is cached as a grant that a later change could leave stale" together with :174, which runs `authorize` (share route included, :57) inside the transaction of each call. Neither path needs a reconnect. The share case relies on the general principle only, and the tests at :177 cover only membership removal (see minor).

account-wide-agent-grant-05.graded_text: An individually shared document gives access to that document only, never to its workspace's other documents or member list, through the UI and the agent alike.

votes.e: docs/workspace-access.md:57 "A share grants exactly one document to exactly one person ... It never grants `workspace.list`, `document.create`, `document.share`, or sight of any other document in that workspace." The gate is shared by every surface: :13 "Every read and write, from the web app, the MCP server, or a background job, goes through the same `authorize` function". On the agent side, :103 returns "`workspace` is `null` for share-only documents". Members are hidden too: :147 "`/w/<id>/members` | Workspace members (Owner/Editor see it...)".

account-wide-agent-grant-06.graded_text: The library shows documents from every workspace the person belongs to by default, with workspace and shared filters held in URL query state, filters only narrow what is shown, and no active-workspace session state is introduced as an authority for browsing or for the agent connection.

votes.e: docs/workspace-access.md:144 "`/documents` | The library: every document the person can reach, across all workspaces and shares". :158 "Filters, in this URL order: `q` (search), `workspace=<id>` (one workspace), `shared=true`". Filters only narrow and the URL grants nothing: :151 "The URL never grants". :103 "`workspace` is an optional filter that only narrows a read". No active-workspace state: :15 "There is no active workspace in session state, cookies, client memory, or token claims". :138 "the app has no 'current workspace' state".

account-wide-agent-grant-07.graded_text: The design introduces no per-seat price and no paid seat gate, and leaves the member cap of 25 as the brief states it. A design that does not discuss billing or the cap passes.

votes.e: docs/workspace-access.md:182 "**Member cap 25** is the same on every plan ... No upgrade is offered at the cap, because no plan raises it." :69 "Plans sell storage, not capabilities. The gate does not ask what plan anyone is on." I checked docs/workspace-access.md and answer.txt for "seat" and found nothing. The closest line is :181, a storage upgrade offered to the Owner, which matches the brief's storage pricing.

blocking: [claude-fallback] Revocation is claimed to be immediate, but the design builds it on an async mirror. docs/workspace-access.md:83 says removal "cuts their agent off from it on the very next call, because membership is read live". Yet :49 reads role "from the provider membership mirror", and :175 says "Membership and roles are owned by the auth provider and mirrored into the database by verified, idempotent webhooks." A late, retried or out-of-order membership.deleted webhook leaves the removed member's agent with access until the mirror catches up. Nothing covers event ordering or reconciling deletes. The test at :177 ("removal from a workspace cuts access on the next call") would only pass if it mutates the DB directly.

[claude-fallback] Agent refusals leak the workspace name to people who only have a share. docs/workspace-access.md:103 promises "`workspace` is `null` for share-only documents, so the agent never learns workspace details the person cannot see". But :193 lets agents reach shared documents "subject to the document's workspace agent policy", and the refusal at :129 is "Acme Studio's owner has turned off access for connected agents". The refusal at :130, "This connection is not set up to reach Acme Studio", has the same problem. A share-only recipient's agent is told the hidden workspace's name.

[claude-fallback] Shared documents and narrowed reach contradict each other. docs/workspace-access.md:65 requires "connection reaches workspace" for every agent call. :63 says the *only these workspaces* list is picked from "my workspaces". A share-only document's workspace can never be on that list. So, as written, any narrowed connection silently loses every shared document, and the design doesn't say whether that is intended.

[claude-fallback] Concurrent edits are left unsafe. docs/workspace-access.md:111 marks `update_document` as replacing the whole content, and :203 defers protection: "Should `update_document` take an expected version to avoid an agent overwriting a person's concurrent edit? Not designed here." Building the design as written lets an agent silently erase a person's concurrent edits.
